note: Efemerides para el boton Tendencias del Studio. Fecha en MM-DD (se repite cada ano). 'angle' es el arquetipo sugerido; 'hook' una cifra o pregunta para abrir. Agregar libremente.

events.title: Battle of Stamford Bridge
events.hook: One Viking held a bridge against an entire army. Then a spear came from below.

events.title: William lands at Pevensey
events.hook: 7,000 men, 700 ships, one landing that changed English forever.

events.title: Proclamation of the People's Republic of China
events.hook: One speech, 300,000 people in the square, a country of 540 million.

events.title: Sputnik 1 launch
events.hook: How did an 83-kg sphere beep its way into panicking a superpower?

events.title: Yom Kippur War begins
events.hook: Two hours. That is how long the Bar Lev line was supposed to hold. It fell in six.

events.title: Columbus reaches the Americas
events.hook: How did three ships cross 5,000 km with a map that was wrong by 15,000?

events.title: Battle of Hastings
events.hook: Why did the shield wall break after nine hours of holding?

events.title: Cuban Missile Crisis begins
events.hook: Thirteen days. One submarine officer said no. That is why you are here.

events.title: Battle of Trafalgar
events.hook: Why did Nelson cut his own line in two to win?

events.title: Battle of Agincourt
events.hook: How did 6,000 archers stop 25,000 knights in a muddy field?

events.title: Charge of the Light Brigade
events.hook: 670 riders, one misread order, twenty minutes.

events.title: Tsar Bomba test
events.hook: They cut the bomb's yield in half so the crew could survive it. It was still 50 megatons.

events.title: Gunpowder Plot
events.hook: 36 barrels under Parliament. How much of London would have gone?

events.title: Fall of the Berlin Wall
events.hook: One official misread a memo on live TV. Hours later the wall was open.

events.title: Armistice of 1918
events.hook: The last soldier died at 10:59. The war ended at 11:00.

events.title: Jonestown
events.hook: 909 people, one afternoon, one radio message that never came.

events.title: Kennedy assassination
events.hook: 8.3 seconds in Dallas. Sixty years of questions.

events.title: Tutankhamun's tomb opened
events.hook: Carter saw 'wonderful things'. It took ten years to empty the room.

events.title: Rosa Parks refuses to give up her seat
events.hook: One seat, 381 days of boycott, 40,000 people walking to work.

events.title: Attack on Pearl Harbor
events.hook: How did 353 aircraft cross 6,000 km of ocean without being seen?

events.title: Battle of the Bulge begins
events.hook: Nuts. One word, one general, one surrounded town.

events.title: Charlemagne crowned emperor
events.hook: A crown placed from behind. He claimed he never saw it coming.

events.title: Caesar crosses the Rubicon
events.hook: One legion, one river 30 meters wide, and the Republic was over.

events.title: Liberation of Auschwitz
events.hook: 7,000 people were left behind. The soldiers who found them had no orders for this.

events.title: Bombing of Dresden
events.hook: 1,300 bombers, 3,900 tons, one night.

events.title: Assassination of Caesar
events.hook: 23 stab wounds. Only one was fatal.

events.title: Titanic sinks
events.hook: Why did a ship built with 16 compartments sink with four flooded?

events.title: Fall of Constantinople
events.hook: How did a 27-foot cannon end a thousand years of walls?

events.title: D-Day
events.hook: How do you hide 7,000 ships from the people watching the coast?

events.title: Moon landing
events.hook: How did a computer with 4 KB of memory land two men on the Moon?

events.title: Hiroshima
events.hook: One man survived Hiroshima, took a train, and was in Nagasaki three days later.

events.title: Eruption of Vesuvius
events.hook: The bodies of Pompeii are not bodies. They are holes.
